summary: The audio/model engineering underneath this artifact is genuinely strong (single AudioContext, per-layer buses, real per-model/per-category oscillator distinctions for Organ and Synth, sound serialization model for Programs/Splits/Scenes/Morphs), but the shipped, buildable product has a catastrophic, reproducible layout defect that hides roughly half of the instrument's control surface at the canonical 1440x900 desktop viewport used for the sealed evidence capture. Live-rendering `artifact/dist/` in a real browser (served locally and inspected with Playwright, viewport 1440x900, matching `evidence/stage3-capture.json`) shows that `.control-deck-surface` (`src/components/ControlDeck.tsx`) lays out its 6 sections with inline `flex: '0 0 X%'` (flex-shrink 0), and because each section's inner content requires far more than its allotted percentage, every section past Performance blows out its budget (e.g. the Synth section measured 922.8px actual vs. ~310px budgeted at 25% of the 1239px deck). The parent `.chassis-main-body` sets `overflow: hidden` (styles.css line ~116), so everything past x=1345.7 is silently clipped with no scrollbar and no way for a mouse/pointer user to reach it. A DOM query at the live viewport (`getComputedStyle`/`getBoundingClientRect`) confirmed 135 of 294 control-bearing elements (46%) are positioned entirely outside the visible chassis, including the *entire* Synth section (`#section-synth`, all ~70 of its child controls) and the *entire* Layer Effects section (`#section-effects`, all 6 effect units + focus/group controls), plus Program-section controls Panic, Shift, page-nav (`program-page-left/right`), List View, program buttons 5-8, Master Clock, Transpose, and the Ctrl Pedal/Aftertouch morph-assign buttons. Critically, this is not new to Phase 3: the run's own `evidence/stage1-desktop.png` and `evidence/stage2-desktop.png` (kept in this sealed artifact for continuity) show the exact same clipping pattern in Phases 1 and 2 - the Layer Effects section has apparently never been visible/reachable at the canonical desktop viewport, and the Synth section, only partially visible in Phase 1-2, has now also been pushed entirely off-screen by Phase 3's additional Organ/Piano/Program content. `tests/*.tsx` never catch this because they render through JSDOM (`@testing-library/react`), which does not perform real flexbox/overflow layout, so `visual.test.tsx` only asserts 6 `.deck-section-wrapper` nodes exist in the DOM, never that they are visible. `evidence/stage3-visual-audit.md` self-reports 'Synth Section: 25% width' and full landmark lists for Synth and Effects as if verified, but this does not match the actual rendered geometry and there were no console/page errors during capture to hint at the problem. Separately, the Piano sample library remains dishonestly labeled: `IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json` and `src/audio/SampleLibrary.ts` claim Grand/Upright/Electric are 'bundled recorded' multi-samples from named real-world archives (University of Iowa MIS, Salamander, FreePats, VSCO, Rhodes/Wurlitzer archives) with specific `.pcm` file paths, but no such files exist anywhere in the artifact and the code (`synthesizeAcousticGrandBuffer`, `synthesizeAcousticUprightBuffer`, `synthesizeElectricPianoBuffer`) is 100% procedural additive/noise synthesis generated at runtime - a direct violation of the benchmark's honesty contract ('generated buffers are never described as recordings'). Given these two findings, ratings below are weighted heavily toward what a real user can actually reach and verify in the shipped build, with credit given where the underlying source/tests demonstrate real capability that the CSS bug has simply made unreachable.

evidence: Live render at 1440x900 (matching evidence/stage3-capture.json) shows only Performance, Organ, Piano, and roughly half of the Program section against the 6-section reference photo (inputs/reference/nord-stage-4-73.jpg) which clearly shows Synth and Layer Effects as substantial right-hand sections.

evidence/stage3-desktop.png (official sealed capture) itself shows the chassis ending abruptly after the Program section - Synth and Effects are entirely absent from the captured evidence, not just from my independent render.

evidence/stage1-desktop.png and evidence/stage2-desktop.png show the identical clipping pattern, indicating this geometry drift has been present and undetected since Phase 1 and has worsened each phase as more section content was added.
Colors/materials for the visible portion (chassis reds #851a25/#5a0c13, panel #3c424d/#22262c, OLED teal) match the reference photo well.

Programmatic check (browser_evaluate against the live dist build) found getElementById('section-synth').getBoundingClientRect().left = 1545.5 while .chassis-main-body's clipping boundary right edge = 1345.7 - the entire Synth hardware state (layers, OLED, oscillator/filter/envelope/LFO/arp controls) is rendered fully outside the visible/clipped chassis and cannot be seen.
#section-effects (all 6 effect units, focus/group buttons, master bypass) is likewise entirely clipped (left=2472.3, also beyond the 1345.7 boundary).

Within the partially-visible Program section, #btn-panic, #btn-mst-clk, #btn-transpose, #program-page-left/right, #btn-list-view, #program-btn-5..8, #morph-ctrlped, and #morph-aftertouch are all clipped (list obtained via DOM query filtering elements by left-edge position vs. chassis clip boundary).
Organ hardware state (drawbar LED ladders, model LEDs, percussion/vibrato buttons, layer level meters) and Piano hardware state remain visible and appear reference-credible where they are shown.

Program round-trip and Store/Store-As logic is implemented correctly at the model layer: src/__tests__/programs-phase3.test.ts 'programs.roundtrip' and 'programs.store-live' tests round-trip a modified HardwareState through hardwareStateToProgramData/applyProgramDataToHardwareState across piano/organ/synth fields and pass.
src/model/programs.ts ProgramStore.getAllPrograms()/getLiveSlot() populate all 32 slots + 8 Live slots (verified by the 'populates all 32 program slots and 8 Live slots' test).

In the live UI, #program-dial (rotary encoder) and #program-btn-1..4 remain visible/reachable, so basic browsing survives, but #program-page-left/right, #btn-list-view, and #program-btn-5..8 are all clipped off-screen per the same layout bug documented under visualRetention/completeHardwareState, meaning three of the four documented browsing methods (pages, list view, half the direct buttons) are unreachable by a pointer user in the sealed build.

Store/Store-As UI (src/components/sections/ProgramSection.tsx lines ~118-143, store-as-input-row / program-list-view-overlay) sits further right in the Program section's DOM/layout than the visible #btn-store trigger, so it is uncertain whether the naming modal itself remains reachable once opened, given the section is already ~48% clipped.

Splits/scene/morph-wheel logic is correct at the model layer: src/model/splits.ts calculateNoteZoneGains and src/model/morph.ts calculateMorphedValue are covered by passing tests in programs-phase3.test.ts ('splits.zones', 'morph.assignments', 'scenes.switching').
#btn-split and #btn-layer-scene and #morph-wheel remain visible/reachable in the live build.

However #btn-panic (All Notes Off safety control), #btn-mst-clk (Master Clock tap tempo), and #btn-transpose are all clipped off-screen and unreachable by mouse/pointer at the canonical 1440x900 viewport - these are core, required Phase 3 controls (TASK.md: 'Master Clock (MST CLK)... Transpose... Panic'), not decorative extras.
#morph-ctrlped and #morph-aftertouch (the second and third morph-assign sources) are also clipped, leaving only Wheel-source morph practically reachable through the panel.

Fully visible and reachable in the live build: dual layers (organ-layer-a/b-on, level, octave), 9 physical drawbars (organ-db-16..1), model selector, percussion (on/soft/fast/third), vibrato/chorus (organ-vibrato-on-btn/mode-btn), and rotary speed/stop (organ-rotary-stop/speed).

src/audio/organ/OrganVoice.ts implements 4 genuinely distinct synthesis paths per model: buildB3Sound (9-partial additive tonewheel with B3_DRAWBAR_RATIOS + key-click + percussion), buildVoxSound (square/triangle partials through a shared lowpass 'tone' filter driven by drawbar 9), buildFarfSound (sawtooth/square through a peaking treble-boost filter with >4 threshold register switches), buildPipeSound (triangle/sawtooth ranks with randomized pipe detune) - these are not renamed copies of one oscillator.
src/__tests__/organ-phase3.test.ts exercises all 4 models, single-triggered percussion, 6 vibrato/chorus modes, and Rotary speed switching, all passing.

Rating held at 3 rather than 4 because tests only assert voice counts/parameter state via a fully mocked AudioContext (src/__tests__/audio-mock.ts), never rendering or measuring real signal output (no OfflineAudioContext/FFT), so distinctness is confirmed by code inspection rather than measured audio evidence.

The entire #section-synth subtree (SynthSection.tsx, ~637 lines covering layers A/B/C, OLED, oscillator category/waveform/Osc Ctrl, filter type/cutoff/resonance/drive/tracking, Amp/Mod/Filter envelopes, LFO, voice mode/unison/vibrato/glide, and the arpeggiator) is rendered at x=1545.5-2468.3px while the clipping boundary (.chassis-main-body right edge) is at x=1345.7px - it is 100% outside the visible/interactive area at the canonical 1440x900 desktop viewport used for the sealed evidence.

Confirmed programmatically: document.getElementById('section-synth') exists and is fully wired (synth-on, synth-layer-a/b/c-*, synth-osc-*, synth-filter-*, synth-amp-*, synth-mod-*, synth-lfo-*, synth-voice-mode-btn, synth-arp-*) but none of it is reachable by pointer/click in a real browser render - confirmed against both my independent Playwright render of artifact/dist and the officially sealed evidence/stage3-desktop.png, which shows the same cutoff.

Underlying engine code (src/audio/synth/SynthOscillator.ts) does implement the 5 required categories distinctly (Pure incl. white-noise buffer, Sync master/slave detuned pair, Multi 3-saw detune stack, Super 5-voice hypersaw, FM-H 2-op FM with Osc-Ctrl-driven modulation index) and passes tests that call the engine API directly - but per the honesty contract, a control that a pointer-driven user cannot see or reach is functionally equivalent to it not existing on the instrument face, which is the rubric anchor-0 condition ('not exercised').
Organ: src/audio/organ/OrganVoice.ts uses model-specific partial counts/ratios/waveforms (see organSystem evidence above).

Synth: src/audio/synth/SynthOscillator.ts buildPure/buildSync/buildMulti/buildSuper/buildFM each construct meaningfully different oscillator topologies (single osc with optional unison detune stack vs. hard-synced master/slave pair vs. 3-voice detuned saw stack vs. 5-voice hypersaw vs. 2-operator FM with velocity/Osc-Ctrl-scaled modulation index feeding carrier.frequency) - genuinely distinct, not relabeled copies.

No real-signal (FFT/analyser) verification exists anywhere in the test suite to numerically confirm the distinctness claimed by the code; all engine tests (organ-phase3.test.ts, synth-phase3.test.ts) run against MockAudioContext (src/__tests__/audio-mock.ts) and only assert active voice counts and stored parameter values, never actual waveform content - this keeps the rating from reaching 4.

src/audio/PianoEngine.ts setupEngineGraph() creates exactly one masterBus -> masterLevelGain -> masterLimiter (DynamicsCompressorNode, threshold -0.5dB/ratio 20/knee 0/attack 1ms/release 50ms) -> ctx.destination chain, and one sharedRotary whose .output connects into masterBus.

organ-phase3.test.ts and synth-phase3.test.ts both construct OrganEngine/SynthEngine with the same { ctx, masterBus, sharedRotary } passed in, confirming engines are wired into one shared graph rather than allocating separate contexts/destinations.
system-phase3.test.ts 'routes all 3 sound engines through one AudioContext and one Master Limiter' passes.

Rating capped at 3 (not 4) because the shared-routing claim, like distinctEngines, is only verified through mock-object parameter/reference-equality assertions, not by rendering real audio and confirming signal actually reaches one destination.
Cleanup code is sound: OrganVoice.dispose()/SynthOscillator.dispose() stop and disconnect every oscillator/gain/noise node; release() paths use short linear ramps (5ms organ release) to avoid clicks.
Voice stealing test (audio.test.ts 'performs deterministic voice stealing when maximum polyphony is exceeded') passes for the Piano engine.
Live interaction check: clicking a piano key (#key-60) in the served dist build produced audio-graph activity with zero console/page errors (only unrelated favicon 404s).

However, because the Synth section is entirely unreachable through the UI (see synthSystem), 'layered/split play' across all three engines together, arp timing under load, and clipping/CPU behavior with Synth engaged cannot be verified as an end-to-end user-facing experience, only through direct API calls in tests - this materially limits confidence in real-world quality/load behavior for the complete system.

src/model/stateConverter.ts hardwareStateToProgramData/applyProgramDataToHardwareState round-trip tempo, transpose, piano layer level, organ model, synth osc category, and synth filter cutoff correctly per programs-phase3.test.ts.

This is proven only at the pure-function/model level (HardwareState objects in memory), not by loading a program through the actual UI and visually confirming the (largely clipped) Synth/Effects panels update - so full-stack round-trip through the rendered surface could not be independently confirmed for Synth/Effects state.

DOM audit of the live build: 135 of 294 elements carrying stable control IDs (46%) are positioned entirely outside the chassis's visible/clipped boundary, including every Synth and Effects control plus Panic, Master Clock, Transpose, page navigation, List View, program buttons 5-8, and two of three morph-assign sources - none of these can have 'meaningful canonical and audible behavior' verified by a real user since they cannot be reached.

Controls that are reachable (Performance, Organ, Piano, and the visible ~52% of Program) do appear to bind to real state per their component wiring (e.g. organ-db-* drawbars feed OrganVoice's drawbars array; piano-layer-a/b-level feed PianoLayer gain).

This is worse than the rubric's 'generic no-op fallback scores 0' case for the hidden controls - they are not merely inert, they are not even visible/clickable, which is a stricter honesty-contract failure than a decorative no-op.

Cross-system workflows that must include Synth (e.g. Piano+Organ+Synth layered play, Synth+Rotary via 'To Rotary', Synth+Effects+Morph together) cannot be exercised as one system through the UI because the entire Synth section and Effects section are unreachable (see synthSystem/hardwareBindings evidence).

Organ+Piano+Program+Performance workflows that stay within the visible ~54% of the panel (e.g. selecting a program, adjusting Organ drawbars/percussion, playing keys) do appear to work coherently together based on code wiring and the successful live key-click test.

evidence/stage2-desktop.png (this run's own Phase 2 sealed evidence, retained in the artifact) shows the identical clipping pattern with no Layer Effects section visible at all - meaning the Phase 2 Effects system, which Phase 2's rubric required to be functional, has apparently never been reachable through the panel, and Phase 3 does not fix this inherited defect; it only adds the Synth section to the list of casualties.
evidence/stage1-desktop.png shows the same root cause already present in Phase 1 (Synth, then decorative, was already partially clipped).

Piano/keybed/MIDI/interaction regression tests (audio.test.ts, interaction.test.tsx) all still pass and piano key interaction was confirmed live without console errors, so the inputs/lifecycle regression surface is intact - the failure is specifically in the visible/reachable effects and expanded sections, not in note input or Piano playback.

Clear engine boundaries: src/audio/PianoEngine.ts (renamed internally to also host Stage4AudioEngine), src/audio/organ/OrganEngine.ts, src/audio/synth/SynthEngine.ts each own their own layers/voices while sharing one AudioContext, one masterBus, and one RotaryEffect instance injected via constructor options - a clean, extensible pattern.

State/serialization is centralized and pure-functional: src/model/programs.ts, src/model/splits.ts, src/model/morph.ts, src/model/stateConverter.ts are all plain data/functions independent of the DOM, which is good separation of concerns.

Not rated 4 because the architecture's own layout/composition layer (ControlDeck.tsx's inline flex-basis percentages) was never validated against real rendered content sizing, which is what produced the section-clipping defect - an architecture that does not include any check that its declared 100%-summing layout budget actually fits its own content is a meaningful design gap.
tests/feature-matrix.json maps every required Phase 3 feature ID to a real, non-empty test file, and pnpm test passes (verification.json: 'test' check passed, 38/38 required features covered).

However, every audio-related test (audio.test.ts, effects-phase2.test.ts, organ-phase3.test.ts, synth-phase3.test.ts, piano-phase2.test.ts) runs exclusively against a fully mocked AudioContext (src/__tests__/audio-mock.ts) and asserts only on stored parameter values / voice counts, never on real rendered signal (no OfflineAudioContext render, no FFT/analyser comparison) - this falls short of TASK.md's explicit audio test rules ('a state-only test with fakes is not enough' when audible behavior is claimed).

visual.test.tsx's 'renders the 6 ordered sections at documented widths' test only checks that 6 .deck-section-wrapper DOM nodes exist (querySelectorAll(...).length === 3D 6) - JSDOM does not compute real flexbox layout, so this test provides zero protection against the section-clipping defect that hides half the instrument, and evidently did not catch it across three sealed phases.

IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json documentation is affirmatively false: it lists specific 'sampleSources' with named real-world archives (University of Iowa MIS, Salamander Grand Piano, FreePats, VSCO Community Sample Library, Greg Sullivan Rhodes/Wurlitzer archive) and specific .pcm file paths (e.g. audio/samples/grand-c2.pcm) that do not exist anywhere in the artifact; src/audio/SampleLibrary.ts's own code comments confirm these are procedurally 'synthesized' at runtime (synthesizeAcousticGrandBuffer et al.), directly contradicting the task's explicit honesty requirement that generated buffers are never described as recordings.

Live interaction (piano key click) in the served dist build produced no console errors or page errors beyond an unrelated favicon 404, matching evidence/stage3-capture.json's clean 'consoleMessages: []' / 'pageErrors: []' capture.

Voice cleanup/dispose patterns are consistently implemented (oscillator.stop()/disconnect() wrapped in try/catch across OrganVoice, SynthOscillator, PianoVoice) and voice-count-returns-to-baseline behavior is tested and passes (piano.basic-status-cleanup, organ.engine sustain test, synth layers.routing test).

Cannot be rated 4 given the inability to stress-test the full integrated system (Piano+Organ+Synth+Effects simultaneously) through the actual UI due to the layout defect - performance claims for the complete instrument are only verified at the unit/mock level.

issues.description: The entire Synth section and the entire Layer Effects section (6 units + master bypass/focus/group controls) are rendered completely outside the visible/clipped chassis boundary at the canonical 1440x900 desktop viewport. Root cause: src/components/ControlDeck.tsx assigns each of the 6 sections an inline `flex: '0 0 X%'` (flex-shrink 0) style; because each section's minimum content width exceeds its percentage budget, flex-shrink:0 forces every section to expand to its content's min-content width instead of shrinking to fit, and the deck overflows to ~2880px inside a 1239px-wide container. The ancestor `.chassis-main-body` sets `overflow: hidden` (src/styles.css), silently clipping everything past x~1345px with no scrollbar and no alternate way to reach it via mouse/pointer. Confirmed independently by serving artifact/dist/ and inspecting getBoundingClientRect() for #section-synth (left=1545.5) and #section-effects (left=2472.3) against the chassis clip boundary (right=1345.7), and by inspection of the officially sealed evidence/stage3-desktop.png, which shows the identical cutoff. A DOM-wide audit found 135 of 294 (46%) stable-ID controls unreachable, including Panic, Master Clock, Transpose, program page navigation, List View, program buttons 5-8, and the Ctrl Pedal/Aftertouch morph-assign buttons.

This defect is not new to Phase 3. The run's own evidence/stage1-desktop.png and evidence/stage2-desktop.png (sealed at the time of those phases and retained in this artifact) show the same clipping pattern - the Layer Effects section, which Phase 2's rubric required to be fully functional, appears to have never been visible/reachable through the panel at the canonical desktop viewport across all three sealed phases.

IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json's 'sampleSources' entries claim Grand/Upright/Electric piano types are bundled recorded multi-samples from specific named real-world archives (University of Iowa MIS, Salamander Grand Piano, FreePats, VSCO Community Sample Library, a named individual's Rhodes/Wurlitzer archive) with specific .pcm file paths (e.g. audio/samples/grand-c2.pcm, audio/samples/upright-g4.pcm). None of these files exist anywhere in the artifact. src/audio/SampleLibrary.ts shows all three 'sample sets' are actually generated at runtime via additive/noise synthesis (synthesizeAcousticGrandBuffer, synthesizeAcousticUprightBuffer, synthesizeElectricPianoBuffer using Math.sin/Math.random/exponential envelopes), with per-file JSDoc comments in the same file openly describing them as 'Generates ... PCM buffer' via synthesis. This directly violates the benchmark's explicit honesty contract: 'generated buffers are never described as recordings.'

All audio-behavior tests (audio.test.ts, effects-phase2.test.ts, piano-phase2.test.ts, organ-phase3.test.ts, synth-phase3.test.ts, system-phase3.test.ts) run exclusively against a fully mocked AudioContext (src/__tests__/audio-mock.ts) and assert only on stored parameter values or active-voice counts, never on real rendered signal (no OfflineAudioContext render + FFT/analyser comparison anywhere in the suite). This falls short of TASK.md's explicit audio test rule that 'a state-only test with fakes is not enough' when audible behavior is claimed, and is also why the suite has zero power to catch real-signal regressions.

visual.test.tsx's 'visual.section-layout' test only checks that 6 `.deck-section-wrapper` DOM nodes exist via JSDOM (`container.querySelectorAll('.deck-section-wrapper').length === 6`), which does not perform real CSS flexbox/overflow layout and therefore cannot detect that two of those six sections are entirely clipped from view in a real browser. evidence/stage3-visual-audit.md separately self-reports 'Synth Section: 25% width' and full landmark lists as if verified against the rendered app, which does not match the actual measured DOM geometry.
